title: A dropped item's empty worktree still holds a lane
what: Either `relay queue drop` of a taken item removes its worktree when it is clean and its branch has no commit beyond the default branch, or the lane count does not count a no-item worktree whose branch has no own commit and no modified file. Pick the one with fewer parts.
why: Owner asked, 30 Oct, how lanes are counted. Checking it, the front found 1 of the 6 counted lanes was the worktree of an item the owner had dropped: no item, no commit beyond master, no change in its files, yet counted as running for up to lane_quiet_hours (3 h) after its last commit. That lane blocked a start while 6 of 6 showed busy.
failing_case: 30 Oct 2026: lanes_state counted wt/test-churn-keeps-fseventsd-at-a-full-cor as running (Lane with slug None); its item was dropped, `git status --porcelain` was empty and `git log master..branch` empty; after `git worktree remove` the count fell from 6 to 5 and a pick appeared.
pass_cases: A test: an item taken, then dropped, with a clean worktree and no own commit: lanes_state does not count it, or the worktree is gone after the drop.
A no-item worktree with an own commit or a modified file still counts while changed within lane_quiet_hours.

said: Как мы вообще можем сказать сколько lane занято, как мы оперируем этими данными, где это хранится, разумно было бы смотреть на занятую очередь задач, вероятно мы так и делаем
